<!-- nrmk-1: body_md -->
We would like to emphasise this new concept of vu-retraction (\Cref{def:vu-retract}). It is a very flexible notion, powerful enough to recover the sobrification of a topological space and usual retracts, but also the diagonal embedding of an object of an ultracategory into its ultrapower, as well as filtered vu-colimit (\Cref{ex:vu-retract}), which play a central role in the theory of accessible categories.
<!-- end nrmk-1 -->
<!-- nrmk-2: body_md -->
It is worth emphasising the proof technique we use to establish these vu-characterisations: we reduce to the 0-dimensional case by looking at the localic reflection of the slices of the topos, which we call the \emph{localic slices} (\Cref{def:loc-slice}). The crucial point is that subhyperconnected morphisms and geometric surjections can be detected on their localic slices (\Cref{rmk:propclass}). We suspect that this proof technique can be used in other contexts.
<!-- end nrmk-2 -->
<!-- lem-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:extend-uf}
    Let $\alpha\subseteq 2^S$ be a collection of subsets of a set $S$. Then $\alpha$ can be extended to an ultrafilter, i.e.,  there exists an ultrafilter $\sigma$ on $S$ such that $(\forall s:\sigma) \ s\in A$ for all $A\in\alpha$, if and only if all the finite intersections of subsets of $S$ in $\alpha$ are non-empty.
<!-- end lem-1 -->
<!-- defn-1: body_md -->
\label{def:final-uf}
    An ultrafilter $\lambda$ on a poset $(L,\leq)$ is said \emph{initial} if it satisfies 
    $(\forall \ell:\lambda)\ \ell\leq \ell_0$
    for each $\ell_0\in L$.
     
    Analogously, $\lambda$ is said \emph{final} if it satisfies $(\forall \ell:\lambda)\ \ell\geq \ell_0$ for each $\ell_0\in L$.
<!-- end defn-1 -->
<!-- lem-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:ext-final-uf}
    A poset $(L,\leq)$ possesses an initial ultrafilter if and only if it is codirected, i.e.,  for any $p,q\in L$ there exists $r\in L$ such that $r\leq p,q$. An analogous proposition is true for final ultrafilters and directed posets.
<!-- end lem-2 -->
<!-- defn-2: body_md -->
\label{def:vucat}
    A \emph{virtual ultracategory} $\mathscr{X}$, or \emph{vu-category} for short, is given by the following data.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item A collection of objects, also called points.                        
        \item For every point $a$ and $\sigma$-family of points $(b_s)_{s:\sigma}$, a \emph{homset} $\mathsf{Hom}^\mathscr{X}_{\sigma}(a,b_s)$ (or $\mathsf{Hom}_{\sigma}(a,b_s)$). Elements $f\in\mathsf{Hom}_\sigma(a,b_s)$ are called \emph{vu-arrows of shape} $\sigma$ or \emph{$\sigma$-arrows} and are denoted $f : a  \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{s:\sigma}}\mkern-2mu} b_s$ or simply
        \[f: a  \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\sigma}}\mkern-2mu}b_s.\]
        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
        
        \item For every point $a$, an \emph{identity} $\star$-arrow $\mathsf{id}_a : a \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\star}}\mkern-2mu}a$. For a vu-arrow $f:a \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\sigma}}\mkern-2mu}b_s$ of shape $\sigma$ and a $\sigma$-family of vu-arrows $(g_s : b_s  \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\tau_s}}\mkern-2mu}c_{s,t})_{s:\sigma}$, a $\sigma$-\emph{composite}
        \[g_s\circ_{\sigma} f : a \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\sigma\cdot\tau_s}}\mkern-2mu}c_{s,t}\]
        that we denote diagrammatically by
        \[a \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle f$};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\sigma}}\mkern-2mu}(b_s \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle g_s$};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\tau_s}}\mkern-2mu}c_{s,t}).\]
        \item\label{diag} For any morphism of ultrafilters $\phi : \tau  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \sigma$ a \emph{reindexing} operation, given by set-maps
        \begin{align*}
            \mathsf{Hom}_\sigma(a,b_s) &   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{Hom}_\tau(a,b_{\phi t}) \\
            f & \mapsto \phi^*f
        \end{align*}
        for each $a$ and $(b_s)_{s:\sigma}$.
         
        The vu-arrow $\phi^*f$ is also called the \emph{thickening} of $f$ along $\phi$. In particular, the thickening of $\mathsf{id}_a$ along the unique map $\sigma   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \star$ is called a \emph{diagonal} of $a$ and is denoted $\delta : a \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\sigma}}\mkern-2mu} a$.
    \end{enumerate}
    The above data is required to satisfy the following properties.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item The identity is neutral and the composition is associative: 
        \[f\circ_{\star} \mathsf{id}_a = f\]
        \[\mathsf{id}_{b_s}\circ_{\sigma} f = f\]
        \[(h_{s,t}\circ_{\tau_s} g_s)\circ_{\sigma} f = h_{s,t}\circ_{\sigma\cdot \tau_s} (g_s\circ_{\sigma} f).\] 
        
        \item The thickening operation is functorial:
        \[{\mathsf{id}_{\sigma}}^*f = f\]
        \[\psi^*(\phi^*f) = (\phi\circ\psi)^*f\]
        that is, it induces functors
        \begin{equation}\tag{$\star$} \label{reindex-functor}
        \begin{split}
            (\mathds{U}/\sigma)^{\mathrm{op}} &  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{Set} \\
            (\phi : \tau  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \sigma) &\mapsto \mathsf{Hom}_\tau(a,b_{\phi t}). 
        \end{split}
        \end{equation}
        for each $a$ and $(b_s)_{s:\sigma}$.
        \item The thickening operation is compatible with the composition: for $f : a \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\sigma}}\mkern-2mu} b_s$ and $(g_s : b_s \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\tau_s}}\mkern-2mu} c_{s,t})_{s:\sigma}$
        \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
            \item for any $\phi : \lambda  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \sigma$ 
            \[g_{\phi \ell}\circ_{\lambda} (\phi^*f) = (\phi\cdot\mathsf{id}_{\tau_s})^*(g_s\circ_{\sigma} f)\]
            where $\phi\cdot\mathsf{id}_{\tau_s} : \lambda\cdot\tau_{\phi \ell}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \sigma\cdot\tau_s$,
            \item and for any $(\psi_s : \kappa_s  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \tau_s)_{s:\sigma}$
            \[({\psi_s}^*g_s)\circ_{\sigma} f = (\mathsf{id}_{\sigma}\cdot\psi_s)^*(g_s\circ_{\sigma} f).\]
            where $\mathsf{id}_{\sigma}\cdot\psi_s : \sigma\cdot\kappa_s  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \sigma\cdot\tau_s$.
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end defn-2 -->
<!-- rmk-1: body_md -->
We opt for a prefix notation for the thickening rather than a suffix one (as in \cite[3.8]{SUJ}) because we think of thickening as post-composing with a ‘virtual diagonal’. For instance, in the vu-category $\mathsf{Set}$, to thicken along $\phi : \sigma   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \tau$ is to post-compose with the (generalised) diagonal $A^\tau \hookrightarrow A^\sigma$.
<!-- end rmk-1 -->
<!-- defn-3: body_md -->
\label{def:taut}
    A vu-arrow $f:a \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\tau}}\mkern-2mu}b_{\phi t}$ is said \emph{reducible along $\phi : \tau   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \sigma$} if $\psi_1^*f = \psi_2^*f$ for all $\psi_1,\psi_2 : \lambda\rightrightarrows \tau$ equalising $\phi$.
    A vu-category $\mathscr{X}$ is said \emph{taut} if any $f:a \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\tau}}\mkern-2mu}b_{\phi t}$ reducible along $\phi$ can uniquely be unthickened along $\phi$, i.e.,  there exists a unique vu-arrow $g:a \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\sigma}}\mkern-2mu}b_s$ such that $f=\phi^*g$.
<!-- end defn-3 -->
<!-- rmk-2: body_md -->
It is worth noting that this condition can be seen as a sheaf condition: tautness means that for any $a$ and $(b_s)_{s:\sigma}$ the above functor \eqref{reindex-functor}
    is a sheaf over $\mathds{U}/\sigma$ for the atomic topology.
     
    This topology has already been considered in \cite{Eliasson} where it is related to a topology over the category of filters. This opens the way to a study of a filter version of vu-categories \cite{Filterization}.
<!-- end rmk-2 -->
<!-- defn-4: body_md -->
\label{def:vucat-of-points}
    We denote by $\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E})$ \emph{the vu-category of points} of a topos $\mathscr{E}$. Its objects are given by points of $\mathscr{E}$, i.e.,  geometric morphisms $p : \mathsf{Set}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathscr{E}$, and vu-arrows from $p$ to $(q_s)_{s:\sigma}$ are given by natural transformations $p^*\Rightarrow\int_{s:\sigma}({q_s}^*)$, i.e.,  families of maps $(p^*E  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \int_{s:\sigma}{q_s}^*E)$ natural in $E\in\mathscr{E}$.
<!-- end defn-4 -->
<!-- lem-3: body_md -->
\label{lemma:taut-sober}
    Let $(A_s)_{s:\sigma}$ be a $\sigma$-family of sets and $\phi : \tau  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \sigma$. The reindexing
    \[\phi^* : \textstyle\int_{s:\sigma}A_s\hookrightarrow\int_{t:\tau}A_{\phi t}\]
    is injective, and its image is described by the $x\in \int_{t:\tau}A_{\phi t}$ such that $\psi_1^*x = \psi_2^*x$ for all pairs of maps $\psi_1,\psi_2 : \lambda\rightrightarrows \tau$ equalising $\phi$.
<!-- end lem-3 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
We first show that $\phi^*$ is injective.
    Let $(a_s)_{s:\sigma}$ and $(b_s)_{s:\sigma}$ be elements of $\int_{s:\sigma}A_s$ with the same image by $\phi^*$, that is, $(a_{\phi t})_{t:\tau} = (b_{\phi t})_{t:\tau}$. Then there is a $\tau$-large set of $t$ such that $a_{\phi t} = b_{\phi t}$; and since $\phi$ sends $\tau$-large sets to $\sigma$-large sets, we get $a_s = b_s$ for $\sigma$-all $s$.
     
    We now prove the characterisation of the image of $\phi^*$. An element in the image clearly satisfies the condition. Conversely, we suppose that $(a_t)\in \int_{t:\tau}A_{\phi t}$ cannot be lifted to $\int_{s:\sigma}A_s$. We choose underlying sets such that $\phi : T  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  S$ is total, and we can check that the collection of subsets $T_0\times_{\phi(T_0)}T_0 \subseteq T \times_S T$, for $T_0$ $\tau$-large, together with the subset $D = \{(t,t')\in T \times_S T\ |\ a_t \neq a_{t'}\}$, satisfies \Cref{lem:extend-uf}. We can thus extend them into an ultrafilter $\lambda$ on $T\times_S T$. The sets $(T_0\times_{\phi(T_0)}T_0)$ ensure that the projections give maps $\psi_1,\psi_2 : \lambda\rightrightarrows \tau$ equalising $\phi$, and the set $D$ ensures that $\psi_1^*(a_t)\neq\psi_2^*(a_t)$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- prop-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:sober-taut}
    Let $\mathscr{E}$ be a topos, its vu-category of points $\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E})$ is taut.
<!-- end prop-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
We take a vu-arrow $f : p  \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\tau}}\mkern-2mu}q_{\phi t}$ in $\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E})$, that is, maps $(f_E : p^*E  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \int_{t:\tau}{q_{\phi t}^*E})$ natural in $E\in\mathscr{E}$, such that $f$ is reducible along $\phi : \tau  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \sigma$ in $\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E})$.
     
    We need to show that for any $\xi\in p^*E$, $f_E(\xi)$ is in the image of $\int_{s:\sigma}{q_s}^*E\hookrightarrow\int_{t:\tau}{q_{\phi t}}^*E$. 
                                                                                                                
     
    The hypothesis that $f$ is reducible along $\phi$ ensures that $\psi_1^*f_E(\xi) = \psi_2^*f_E(\xi)$ for all $\psi_1,\psi_2 : \lambda\rightrightarrows \tau$ equalising $\phi$, and we conclude with \Cref{lemma:taut-sober}.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- defn-5: body_md -->
A \emph{vu-sheaf} over a vu-category $\mathscr{X}$ is a vu-functor $A : \mathscr{X}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{Set}$. We denote by $\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})\coloneqq\mathsf{vuCAT}(\mathscr{X},\mathsf{Set})$ the category of vu-sheaves over $\mathscr{X}$.
<!-- end defn-5 -->
<!-- nota-1: body_md -->
For $A$ a vu-sheaf over $\mathscr{X}$ and $p$ a point of $\mathscr{X}$, the set $A(p)$ will also be denoted by $A_p$. For a vu-arrow $f : p \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\sigma}}\mkern-2mu}q_s$ and $\xi\in A_p$, the $\sigma$-family $A(f)(\xi)\in\int_{\sigma}A_{q_s}$ will also be denoted by $f_*\xi$.
<!-- end nota-1 -->
<!-- ex-1: body_md -->
For $E\in\mathscr{E}$, we define the vu-sheaf $\mathsf{ev}(E)\in\mathsf{Sh}(\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E}))$ on the vu-category of points of $\mathscr{E}$ by $\mathsf{ev}(E)(p) \coloneqq p^*E$. This construction induces a functor of categories $\mathscr{E}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{Sh}(\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E}))$ (see \cite[5.2]{Saa}).
<!-- end ex-1 -->
<!-- rmk-3: body_md -->
The term \emph{bounded} is used in \cite[5.8]{Saa} and is inspired by the analogue notion for Garner's ionad \cite[3.7]{IonadGarner}. We would however prefer an intrinsic notion of \emph{small generated vu-category} that can be directly seen on the vu-category (by opposition to boundedness that is seen on the category of vu-sheaves) and that would in particular imply boundedness. Such a notion does not exist yet, and as the present paper focus on the relation between vu-categories and toposes, the notion of boundedness will be sufficient.
<!-- end rmk-3 -->
<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:reconstruction}
    The 2-functor $\mathsf{pt} : \mathsf{Topos}   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{vuCAT}$ corestricts to bounded vu-categories and is right adjoint to $\mathsf{Sh} : \mathsf{vuCat_{b}}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{Topos}$; moreover, this 2-adjunction is pseudo-idempotent and the fixed points on the $\mathsf{Topos}$ side are precisely the toposes with enough points.
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- defn-6: body_md -->
\label{def:enough-sheaves}
    A class of vu-sheaves over $\mathscr{X}$ is said \emph{to separate vu-arrows}, if for parallel vu-arrows $f,g$ in $\mathscr{X}$ to be equal, it is enough to check that $A_f = A_g$ on the vu-sheaves $A$ in the class.
     
    A vu-category is said to \emph{have enough sheaves} if the class of all vu-sheaves over it separates vu-arrows.
<!-- end defn-6 -->
<!-- rmk-4: body_md -->
\label{rmk:enough-sheaves-unit}
    For a bounded vu-category $\mathscr{X}$ having enough sheaves is equivalent to $\eta_\mathscr{X} : \mathscr{X}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{pt}(\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X}))$ being faithful. We will see in \Cref{locsobercaract} that, assuming $\mathscr{X}$ is taut, this is equivalent to the a priori stronger condition of $\eta_\mathscr{X} : \mathscr{X}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{pt}(\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X}))$ being fully faithful.
<!-- end rmk-4 -->
<!-- ex-2: body_md -->
\label{counterex}
    Not every vu-category has enough sheaves; we give here a toy example of such a vu-category without enough sheaves. Take $K$ a non-trivial connected compact Hausdorff topological space, for example the unit interval. We consider $\mathscr{X}$ the vu-category with two objects $a$ and $b$ and $\mathsf{Hom}_\sigma(a,b) \coloneqq \mathsf{pt}(K)$ the underlying set of $K$ for any ultrafilter $\sigma$, and for $(x_s)_{s:\sigma}$ in $K$, the composite
    \[a \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle \delta$};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\sigma}}\mkern-2mu}(a \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle x_s$};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\tau_s}}\mkern-2mu}b) \text{ given by } a \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle y$};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\sigma\cdot\tau_s}}\mkern-2mu}b\]
    where $y$ is the limit of $(x_s)_{s:\sigma}$ in $K$.
    One can check that this data is enough to define the vu-category $\mathscr{X}$ and that a vu-sheaf over $\mathscr{X}$ corresponds to the data of two sets $A$ and $B$ and a continuous map from $K$ into $B^A$ (with the product topology of $B$ seen as a discrete space). But as $K$ is connected and $B^A$ is totally disconnected, such a continuous map is always constant. Hence $\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})$ is the Sierpiński topos $\mathsf{Set}^{[1]}$, where $[1]$ denotes the walking arrow category. Hence, the unit $\eta_\mathscr{X} : \mathscr{X}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{pt}(\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})) = [1]$ identifies together all parallel vu-arrows of $\mathscr{X}$.
<!-- end ex-2 -->
<!-- nota-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:Lref-adjoint}
    We denote by $\iota: \mathsf{Loc} \hookrightarrow \mathsf{Topos}$ the 2-fully faithful 2-functor sending a locale to its topos of sheaves. The assignment $\mathscr{E} \mapsto \mathsf{Sub}_\mathscr{E}(1)$ induces a 2-functor $|-|: \mathsf{Topos}   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathsf{Loc}$ which is left adjoint to $\iota$. In other words, we get the following 2-reflection:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
    \[\begin{tikzcd}[sep = 40pt]
    	\mathsf{Loc} & \mathsf{Topos}.
    	\arrow[""{name=0, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, "\iota"', shift right, hook, from=1-1, to=1-2]
    	\arrow[""{name=1, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, "|-|"'{pos=0.45}, shift right, curve={height=6pt}, from=1-2, to=1-1]
    	\arrow["\dashv"{anchor=center, rotate=-91}, draw=none, from=1, to=0]
    \end{tikzcd}\]
<!-- end nota-2 -->
<!-- defn-7: body_md -->
A vu-category $\mathscr{X}$ is \emph{posetal} if each $\mathsf{Hom}_\sigma(p, q_s)$ is a subsingleton, we write $p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\sigma}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} q_s$ if this set is inhabited. A \emph{vu-poset} is a posetal vu-category, the full subcategory of $\mathsf{vuCAT}$ of vu-posets (resp. essentially small vu-posets) is denoted by $\mathsf{vuPOS}$ (resp. $\mathsf{vuPos}$).
<!-- end defn-7 -->
<!-- defn-8: body_md -->
Let $X$ be a topological space. Write $p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\sigma}}^{{X}}\mkern-2mu} q_s$, and we say that \emph{$(q_s)_{s:\sigma}$ converges to $p$}, when $p \in U$ implies $(\forall s:\sigma)\ q_s \in U$ for each open $U$ of $X$.
<!-- end defn-8 -->
<!-- rmk-5: body_md -->
\label{reconstruction-thm-topo}
    The reconstruction theorem (\Cref{thm:reconstruction}), restricted to this context, identifies sheaves over a topological space and vu-sheaves over the associated vu-poset. Two different direct proofs of this result can be found in \cite[5.4]{Saa} and in \cite[5.7]{Hamad2}.
<!-- end rmk-5 -->
<!-- prop-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:opens-are-upsets}
    Let $X$ be a topological space, then a subset $A$ of $X$ is open if and only if $p \in A$ and $p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\sigma}}^{{X}}\mkern-2mu} q_s$ implies $(\forall s:\sigma)\ q_s \in A$.
<!-- end prop-2 -->
<!-- prop-3: body_md -->
Let $X$ be a topological space, $p$ and $(q_s)_{s:\sigma}$ points of $X$, and $\phi : \tau   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \sigma$. Then $p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\tau}}^{{X}}\mkern-2mu} q_{\phi t}$ implies $p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\sigma}}^{{X}}\mkern-2mu} q_s$.
<!-- end prop-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
It is enough to see that for any subset $U$ of $X$, $(\forall t:\tau)\ q_{\phi t}\in U$ if and only if $(\forall s:\sigma)\ q_{s}\in U$. And both these conditions are equivalent to $U$ being large for the ultrafilter $q_*(\phi_*(\tau)) = q_*(\sigma)$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- prop-4: body_md -->
\label{def:taut-poset}
    A vu-poset $(X, \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu})$ is taut if and only if its vu-inequalities can always be unthickened as much as possible, i.e.,  if $p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\tau}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} q_{\phi t}$ implies $p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\sigma}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} q_s$ for $\phi : \tau   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \sigma$.
<!-- end prop-4 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
It is enough to notice that in a vu-poset, a vu-arrow $f: a \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\tau}}\mkern-2mu}b_{\phi t}$ is always reducible along $\phi : \tau  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \sigma$.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- defn-9: body_md -->
\label{def:open}
    An \emph{open}, also called an \emph{upset}, $U$ of a vu-poset $X$ is a subposet of $X$ such that if $p \in U$ and $p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\sigma}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} q_s$ then $q_s \in U$ for all $s : \sigma$. We denote by $\mathcal{O}(X)$ the poset of opens of $X$.
     
    Similarly, a subposet $F$ of $X$ is \emph{closed} if it is downward-closed, that is, if $p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\sigma}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} q_s$ and $(\forall s:\sigma)\ q_s\in F$ imply $p \in F$.
     
    And the \emph{closure} of a collection $A$ of points of a vu-poset $X$, denoted by $\operatorname{\mathsf{cl}}(A)$, is the collection of $p\in X$ such that there exists an ultrafamily $(a_s)_{s:\sigma}$ of points in $A$ such that $p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\sigma}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} a_s$.
<!-- end defn-9 -->
<!-- rmk-6: body_md -->
The collection of opens of a vu-poset is not necessarily small, for instance those of a large discrete vu-poset. We will have more to say about vu-posets which possess only a set's worth of opens later.
<!-- end rmk-6 -->
<!-- lem-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:smallest-closedset}
    Let $A$ be a collection of points of a vu-poset $X$, $\operatorname{\mathsf{cl}}(A)$ is the smallest closed subposet of $X$ containing $A$.
<!-- end lem-4 -->
<!-- lem-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:closure}
                                                                                                   
    Let $A$ be a collection of points of a vu-poset $X$, a point $p\in X$ belongs to $\operatorname{\mathsf{cl}}(A)$ if and only if every open $U \subseteq X$ which contains $p$ intersects $A$.
<!-- end lem-5 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
If $p\in\operatorname{\mathsf{cl}}(A)$, then $p \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\sigma}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu}a_s$ for some $(a_s)_{s:\sigma}$ in $A$, and so any open $U$ containing $p$ contains the $(a_s)$ and so intersects $A$. Conversely if $p\notin\operatorname{\mathsf{cl}}(A)$, then $X\setminus\operatorname{\mathsf{cl}}(A)$ is an open containing $p$ that does not intersect $A$.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- prop-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:Barr}
    Let $X$ be a vu-poset. If $p$ and $(q_s)_{s \in \sigma}$ in $X$ are such that every open $U$ of $X$ which contains $p$ also contains $(q_s)_{s\in\sigma}$, then $p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\tau}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} q_{\phi t}$ for some thickening $\phi : \tau   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \sigma$.
<!-- end prop-5 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
We fix $S$ an underlying set of $\sigma$.
    
    First, we notice that if $\ell \subseteq S$ is $\sigma$-large then $p \in \operatorname{\mathsf{cl}}(\{q_s : s \in \ell\})$. Indeed, if an upset $U$ contains $p$ then $\{s \in \ell : q_s \in U\}$ is $\sigma$-large as the intersection of two large sets, hence non-empty --- thus  \Cref{lem:closure} ensures $p \in \operatorname{\mathsf{cl}}(\{q_s : s \in \ell\})$. Hence we get some $(s^\ell_t \in \ell)_{t:\tau_{\ell}}$ such that \[p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\tau_{\ell}}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} q_{s^\ell_t}.\]

    Using \ref{lem:ext-final-uf}, we can consider an initial ultrafilter $\lambda$ on the codirected poset of $\sigma$-large sets; we can thus merge the above $(s^\ell_t)\in S^{\tau_\ell}$ together along $\lambda$ into the family
    \[\phi \coloneqq (s^\ell_t)_{(\ell,t) : \tau} \in S^\tau\]
    where $\tau\coloneqq\lambda\cdot\tau_\ell$.
    
    We show it is a thickening of $\sigma$, i.e.,  that $\phi_*(\tau) = \sigma$.
    It is enough to show, for each $\sigma$-large $\ell_0\subseteq S$, that $(\forall (\ell,t) : \tau)\ \phi{(\ell,t)}\in \ell_0$, i.e.,  that
    \[(\forall \ell : \lambda)\ (\forall t : \tau_\ell)\ s^\ell_t\in \ell_0,\]
    and for $\ell: \lambda$, we can assume $\ell\subseteq \ell_0$ by initiality of $\lambda$, and then for $t:\tau_\ell$ we have $s^{\ell}_t \in \ell \subseteq \ell_0$ as desired.
                                                                                                                                                                                                         
    
    Hence, $\phi$ induces a map $\phi:\tau  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \sigma$, and the composite
    \[p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\ell:\lambda}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} (p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{t:\tau_{\ell}}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} q_{s^{\ell}_t})\]
    gives $p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\ell:\lambda\cdot t:\tau_\ell}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} q_{s^{\ell}_t}$, i.e.,  $p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{(\ell,t):\tau}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} q_{\phi(\ell,t)}$ as wanted.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- rmk-7: body_md -->
We should stress the importance of this proposition as it enables us to get a vu-inequality (and thus a vu-arrow) from an assumption on the opens. This result is already essentially in \cite{Barr}, and will be categorified later in \Cref{prop:Barr-categorified} (see also \Cref{rmk:Barr-categorified}).
<!-- end rmk-7 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:Barr-taut} \label{cor:poset-iso-points}
    For $p$ and $(q_s)_{s:\sigma}$ points of a taut vu-poset, $p \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\sigma}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu}q_s$ if and only if every open containing $p$ also contains $(q_s)_{s:\sigma}$. In particular, two points of a taut vu-poset which belong to the same opens are isomorphic.
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Suppose that every open containing $p$ also contains $(q_s)_{s:\sigma}$, then \Cref{prop:Barr} gives us $p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\sigma}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} q$ and $q  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\tau}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} p$, and by tautness of the vu-poset (\Cref{def:taut-poset}) we deduce $p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\star}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} q$ and $q  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\star}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} p$.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- cor-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:small-vu-pos}
    For $X$ a taut vu-poset, the following conditions are equivalent,
    \begin{enumerate}      
        \item $X$ has a set's worth of opens; \label{cond:poset-small-opens}
        \item $X$ is essentially small; \label{cond:poset-small}
        \item $X$ belongs to the essential image of $\mathsf{TopSp}$. \label{cond:poset-TopSp}
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end cor-2 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
By \Cref{cor:poset-iso-points}, the isomorphism class of a point of $X$ is completely determined by the way it lies in the opens of $X$. If \ref{cond:poset-small-opens} holds, then there is at most a set's worth of ways to lie in the opens, and thus the isomorphism classes of $X$ form a set, i.e.,  \ref{cond:poset-small} holds.
     
    If \ref{cond:poset-small} holds, we can suppose up to equivalence that $X$ is a small taut vu-poset. Then the upsets on $X$ define a topology on the set of points of $X$ and \Cref{cor:Barr-taut} shows that $X$ is the vu-poset of points of this topological space, i.e.,  \ref{cond:poset-TopSp} holds.
     
    Finally, {\ref{cond:poset-TopSp} $\Rightarrow$ \ref{cond:poset-small-opens}} follows from \Cref{prop:opens-are-upsets}.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- defn-10: body_md -->
\label{def:Tref}
    Let $\mathscr{X}$ be a vu-category, its \emph{topological reflection}, denoted by $|\mathscr{X}|$, is the vu-poset on the objects of $\mathscr{X}$ where $p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\sigma}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu}q_s$ if there exists a vu-arrow $p  \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\tau}}\mkern-2mu} q_{\phi t}$ in $\mathscr{X}$ for some thickening $\phi : \tau   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \sigma$.
<!-- end defn-10 -->
<!-- prop-6: body_md -->
The topological reflection $|\mathscr{X}|$ is taut and the natural vu-functor $\mathscr{X}   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  |\mathscr{X}|$ is universal among vu-functors from $\mathscr{X}$ into a taut vu-poset, that is, for a taut vu-poset $X$, any vu-functor $\mathscr{X}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  X$ factorises uniquely trough $\mathscr{X}   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  |\mathscr{X}|$.
<!-- end prop-6 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
Suppose $p \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\tau}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu}q_{\phi t}$ in $|\mathscr{X}|$ for some thickening $\phi : \tau  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \sigma$. This means that there exists a vu-arrow $p \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\lambda}}\mkern-2mu}q_{\psi \phi \ell}$ for some $\psi : \lambda  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \tau$, and thus $p \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\sigma}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu}q_s$ in $|\mathscr{X}|$. Hence, by \Cref{def:taut-poset}, $|\mathscr{X}|$ is taut.

    We now show the universal property. Let $X$ be a taut vu-poset; we show that any vu-functor $\mathscr{X}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  X$ factorises uniquely through $\mathscr{X}   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  |\mathscr{X}|$. The uniqueness follows from the fact that a functor into a vu-poset is determined by its behaviour on the objects and that $\mathscr{X}   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  |\mathscr{X}|$ is surjective on objects.
     
    We take a vu-functor $F : \mathscr{X}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  X$ and we show that $F$ induces a map of vu-posets $|\mathscr{X}|  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu

    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  X$, i.e.,  that $p \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\sigma}}^{{|\mathscr{X}|}}\mkern-2mu}q_s$ implies $F(p) \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\sigma}}^{{X}}\mkern-2mu}F(q_{s})$.
     
    By definition, $p \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\sigma}}^{{|\mathscr{X}|}}\mkern-2mu} q_s$ gives some map $\phi:\tau  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{

    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \sigma$ and some $p \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\tau}}\mkern-2mu}q_{\phi t}$ in $\mathscr{X}$, hence $F(p) \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\tau}}^{{X}}\mkern-2mu}F(q_{\phi t})$, and by \Cref{def:taut-poset} we have $F(p) \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\sigma}}^{{X}}\mkern-2mu}F(q_{s})$.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- prop-7: body_md -->
\label{circular-square}
    Let $\mathscr{X}$ be a bounded vu-category, $\mathcal{O}(|\mathscr{X}|) \cong |\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})|$.
<!-- end prop-7 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
We denote by $[1]$ the taut vu-poset corresponding to the Sierpiński space, so that
    \[\mathcal{O}(|\mathscr{X}|)\cong\mathsf{vuCat}(|\mathscr{X}|,[1])\cong\mathsf{vuCat}(\mathscr{X},[1])\cong\mathsf{Sub}_{\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})}(1) \cong |\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})|.\qedhere\]
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- prop-8: body_md -->
\label{prop:Tref-adjoint}
    If moreover $\mathscr{X}$ is bounded, we can identify $|\mathscr{X}|$ with a topological space, and the assignment $\mathscr{X} \mapsto |\mathscr{X}|$ extends to a 2-functor $|-| : \mathsf{vuCat_{b}}   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathsf{TopSp}$ that is left adjoint to the inclusion $\iota : \mathsf{TopSp} \hookrightarrow \mathsf{vuCat_{b}}$, i.e.,  we have a 2-reflection:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
    	\mathsf{TopSp} & \mathsf{vuCat_{b}}.
    	\arrow[""{name=0, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, "\iota"',shift right, hook, from=1-1, to=1-2]
    	\arrow[""{name=1, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, "|-|"', shift right, curve={height=6pt}, from=1-2, to=1-1]
    	\arrow["\dashv"{anchor=center, rotate=-90}, draw=none, from=1, to=0]
    \end{tikzcd}\]
<!-- end prop-8 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
We suppose $\mathscr{X}$ bounded. By \Cref{circular-square} $|\mathscr{X}|$ has a set's worth of opens, and by \Cref{prop:small-vu-pos} it can be identified to a topological space.
     
    The 2-functoriality and the reflection are straightforward.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- rmk-8: body_md -->
Although we defined $|\mathscr{X}|$ for all vu-categories, we only consider it as a functor on $\mathsf{vuCat_{b}}$ and not on $\mathsf{vuCAT}$.
    This restriction to bounded vu-categories is only here to ensure that the reflection functor lands in $\mathsf{TopSp}$ and not in some category of ``large'' topological spaces.
    That being said, it is worth noting that the adjunction of \Cref{prop:Tref-adjoint} is purely algebraic: $|-| : \mathsf{vuCAT}   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathsf{vuPOS_{taut}}$ is left adjoint to the inclusion $\mathsf{vuPOS_{taut}}   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->,inj] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathsf{vuCAT}$, and that, if $X$ is a vu-poset, the reflection $X  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} |X|$ can be seen as the \emph{tautification} of the vu-poset $X$.
<!-- end rmk-8 -->
<!-- prop-9: body_md -->
\label{prop:rpt=ptr}
    The vu-functor between vu-posets $|\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E})|   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathsf{pt}(|\mathscr{E}|)$ is fully faithful.
<!-- end prop-9 -->
<!-- rmk-9: body_md -->
Note however that $|\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E})|   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathsf{pt}(|\mathscr{E}|)$ is not necessarily an equivalence: a point of $|\mathscr{E}|$ does not necessarily come from a point of $\mathscr{E}$. For example, $\mathscr{E}$ may be a hyperconnected topos (so $\mathsf{pt}(|\mathscr{E}|) = 1$) with no points (so $|\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E})|$ is the empty space). The existence of such a topos follows from \cite[3.4.14 and 3.5.4]{johnstone:elephant}.
<!-- end rmk-9 -->
<!-- defn-11: body_md -->
A vu-functor $F : \mathscr{A}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathscr{X}$ is said \emph{étale} if all its fibres $F^{-1}\{p\}\coloneqq \{a\in\mathscr{A} \ | \ F(a) = p\}$ are small, and if any $g : F(a) \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\sigma}}\mkern-2mu}q_s$ has a unique lift, i.e.,  there exists a unique vu-arrow $f : a \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\sigma}}\mkern-2mu}b_s$ in $\mathscr{A}$ such that $F(f) = g$. We will write $g_*(a)$ or $g_*a$ for the family $(b_s)_{s:\sigma}$.
<!-- end defn-11 -->
<!-- nota-3: body_md -->
The total space of a vu-sheaf $A,B,\dots$ above $\mathscr{X}$ will be systematically denoted by the corresponding letter $\mathscr{A},\mathscr{B},\dots$, or by $\mathrm{\acute{E}t}_{A}, \mathrm{\acute{E}t}_{B}, \dots$ if we need to be explicit.
<!-- end nota-3 -->
<!-- lem-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:slice-etale}
    Let $F : \mathscr{B}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathscr{A}$ and $G:\mathscr{A}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathscr{X}$ be two vu-functors,
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item if $F$ and $G$ are étale, so is $G\circ F$,
        \item if $G\circ F$ and $G$ are étale, so is $F$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-6 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item The fibre $(G\circ F)^{-1}\{p\} = \bigsqcup_{a\in G^{-1}\{p\}} F^{-1}\{a\}$ is small as a small union of small sets, and the unique lifting properties compose well.
        \item The fibre $F^{-1}\{a\}$ is small as a subset of $(G\circ F)^{-1}\{F(a)\}$, and the unique lifting of some $f : F(x) \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{

 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\sigma}}\mkern-2mu} b_s$ is given by the unique lifting of $G(f) : G\circ F(x) \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu

<!-- lem-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:fully faithful general}
    Let $L : \mathscr{D}   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathscr{C}$ be a functor between categories having a fully faithful right adjoint, and let $F,G : \mathscr{C}   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathscr{A}$ be two functors to another category $\mathscr{A}$. For any natural transformation $\beta : FL \Rightarrow GL$ there exists a unique natural transformation $\alpha : F \Rightarrow G$ such that $\alpha L = \beta$.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	\mathscr{D} && \mathscr{C} && \mathscr{A}
	\arrow[""{name=0, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, "L", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow[""{name=1, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, shift left=3, curve={height=-30pt}, from=1-1, to=1-5]
	\arrow[""{name=2, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, shift right=3, curve={height=30pt}, from=1-1, to=1-5]
	                                                                                                                       
	\arrow[""{name=4, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, "F"{description}, shift left=2, curve={height=-12pt}, from=1-3, to=1-5]
	\arrow[""{name=5, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, "G"{description}, shift right=2, curve={height=12pt}, from=1-3, to=1-5]
	                                                                    
	\arrow["{\forall \beta}"{pos=0.2}, shift right=8, between={0.1}{0.9}, crossing over, Rightarrow, from=1, to=2]
	\arrow["{\exists!\alpha}", between={0.2}{0.8}, Rightarrow, dashed, from=4, to=5]
\end{tikzcd}\]
<!-- end lem-7 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
We denote $R:\mathscr{C}\hookrightarrow\mathscr{D}$ the right adjoint of $L$.
    
    Suppose such an $\alpha$ exists. Since $R$ is fully faithful, the counit $\varepsilon_C : L R(C)   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  C$ is an isomorphism. The naturality square it induces forces $\alpha$ to be $(G\varepsilon) \circ (\beta R) \circ (F\varepsilon)^{-1}$, thus $\alpha$ is unique.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
    	{F(L R(C))} & {F(C)} \\
    	{G(L R(C))} & {G(C)}
    	\arrow["{F\varepsilon_C}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
    	\arrow[""{name=0, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, "{\alpha_{L R(C)}}", shift left=2, from=1-1, to=2-1]
    	\arrow[""{name=1, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, "{\beta_{R(C)}}"', shift right=2, from=1-1, to=2-1]
    	\arrow["{\alpha_C}", from=1-2, to=2-2]
    	\arrow["{G\varepsilon_C}"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
    	\arrow[between={0.3}{0.7}, equals, from=0, to=1]
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    
    Of course, the above square can just as well be taken as a definition of $\alpha$, which would settle existence provided that this definition satisfies $\alpha_{L D} = \beta_D$ for each $D \in \mathscr{D}$. For this, one needs only to paste the defining square for $\alpha_{L D}$ with the naturality square of $\beta$ at the unit $\eta_D$, noting that the long edges are identity morphisms due to the triangle identities of $L \dashv R$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
	{FL(D)} & {FLRL(D)} & {FL(D)} \\
	{GL(D)} & {GLRL(D)} & {GL(D)}
	\arrow["{FL\eta_D}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{=}"{description}, curve={height=-22pt}, dotted, no head, from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{\beta_D}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{F\varepsilon_{L D}}", from=1-2, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{\beta_{RL D}}"{description}, from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{\alpha_{L D}}", from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{GL\eta_D}"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{=}"{description}, curve={height=22pt}, dotted, no head, from=2-1, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{G\varepsilon_{L D}}"', from=2-2, to=2-3]
    \end{tikzcd}\qedhere\]
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- thm-3: body_md -->

<!-- defn-12: body_md -->
In a category, an object $A$ is a \emph{subquotient} of an object $B$ if it is a quotient of a subobject of $B$, i.e.,  if there exists a span $B \hookleftarrow C \twoheadrightarrow A$ whose left leg is a monomorphism and whose right leg is an epimorphism.
<!-- end defn-12 -->
<!-- rmk-10: body_md -->
\label{rem_subquotient-order}
    In a category where monomorphisms and epimorphisms are stable under pullbacks and pushouts, such as a topos, the order does not matter: every quotient of a subobject of $B$ is a subobject of a quotient of $B$ and vice versa.
<!-- end rmk-10 -->
<!-- lem-8: body_md -->
\label{lem_localic}
    Suppose that $\mathscr{C}$ is a category and that $\mathscr{X}$ is a collection of objects of $\mathscr{C}$ such that any object of $\mathscr{C}$ is a subquotient of an element of $\mathscr{X}$. Let $F,G : \mathscr{C}   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathscr{D}$ be two functors such that $F$ preserves epimorphisms and $G$ preserves monomorphisms and take $\alpha, \beta : F \Rightarrow G$ two natural transformations between them.
    If $\alpha_X = \beta_X$ for every $X \in \mathscr{X}$, then $\alpha = \beta$.
<!-- end lem-8 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Pick $C \in \mathscr{C}$. By assumption there exist a monomorphism $m : A \hookrightarrow X$ with $X \in \mathscr{X}$ and an epimorphism $e : A \twoheadrightarrow C$. Consider the naturality squares of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ for $m : A \hookrightarrow X$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
    	{F(A)} && {F(X)} \\
    	\\
    	{G(A)} && {G(X)}
    	\arrow["{F(m)}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
    	\arrow["{\alpha_A}"', shift right=2, from=1-1, to=3-1]
    	\arrow["{\beta_A}", shift left=2, from=1-1, to=3-1]
    	\arrow[""{name=0, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, "{\beta_X}", shift left=2, from=1-3, to=3-3]
    	\arrow[""{name=1, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, "{\alpha_X}"', shift right=2, from=1-3, to=3-3]
    	\arrow["{G(m)}", hook, from=3-1, to=3-3]
    	\arrow[between={0.2}{0.8}, equals, from=1, to=0]
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    From $\alpha_X = \beta_X$ it follows that $G(m) \circ \alpha_A = G(m) \circ \beta_A$, but $G(m)$ is a monomorphism by assumption, so $\alpha_A = \beta_A$.
    By the same reasoning on the naturality square of $e : A \twoheadrightarrow C$, together with the fact that $F$ preserves epimorphisms, it follows that $\alpha_C = \beta_C$, so that $\alpha = \beta$.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- rmk-11: body_md -->
In a setting where \Cref{rem_subquotient-order} applies, the proposition remains true if the preservation properties are swapped.
<!-- end rmk-11 -->
<!-- thm-4: body_md -->
\label{thm-loc}
    Let $f : \mathscr{E}   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathscr{F}$ be a localic geometric morphism, then $\mathsf{pt}(f) : \mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E})   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{F})$ is \emph{faithful}.
<!-- end thm-4 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Suppose that $\alpha, \beta$ are two $\sigma$-arrows $p  \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\sigma}}\mkern-2mu}q_s$ in $\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E})$ which have the same image under $\mathsf{pt}(f)$.
    This means that $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are two natural transformations $p^*\Rightarrow \int_{s:\sigma}{q_s}^*$ that agree on objects of the form $f^*(X)$ with $X \in \mathscr{F}$.
     
    The functor $p^*$ is a left adjoint, so it preserves epimorphisms. Both $\int_{s:\sigma}$ and $({q_s}^*)$ preserve finite limits, so they preserve monomorphisms as well. \Cref{lem_localic} therefore applies and yields $\alpha = \beta$.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- defn-13: body_md -->
\label{def:loc-slice}
    For a geometric morphism $f : \mathscr{F}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathscr{E}$ and $E\in\mathscr{E}$, \emph{the localic slice} of $f$ above $E$ is the morphism of locales given by $|f/E| : |\mathscr{F}/f^*E|   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} |\mathscr{E}/E|$.
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
    	{\mathscr{F}/f^*E} & {\mathscr{E}/E} \\
    	\mathscr{F} & \mathscr{E}
    	\arrow["{f/E}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
    	\arrow["{\text{ét}}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
    	\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-1, to=2-2]
    	\arrow["{\text{ét}}", from=1-2, to=2-2]
    	\arrow["f", from=2-1, to=2-2]
    \end{tikzcd}\]
<!-- end defn-13 -->
<!-- rmk-12: body_md -->
\label{rmk:propclass}
    We propose to say that a class of geometric morphisms is \emph{propositional} if a geometric morphism belongs to the class if and only if all its localic slices belong to the class.
     
    As we will see later (\Cref{prop:surj-prop} and \Cref{shc-localic}), (sub)hyperconnected and surjective geometric morphisms form propositional classes of geometric morphisms. This is the crucial property that we will use to establish their vu-categorical characterisations, and we expect that the techniques presented in this paper can be extended to other propositional classes of geometric morphisms.
<!-- end rmk-12 -->
<!-- prop-10: body_md -->
\label{prop:loc-slice}
    For $F:\mathscr{X}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathscr{Y}$ between bounded vu-categories and $B\in\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{Y})$, the localic slice of $\mathsf{Sh}(F)$ above $B$ is given by 
    \[\mathcal{O}(|F^*\mathscr{B}|)   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathcal{O}(|\mathscr{B}|).\]
<!-- end prop-10 -->

By \Cref{thm:etale}\ref{prop:slice-etale} the localic slice is given by $|\mathsf{Sh}(F^*\mathscr{B})|   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{

 \mkern-1mu}  |\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{B})|$ and by \Cref{circular-square} this map can be rewritten as $\mathcal{O}(|F^*\mathscr{B}|)   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{

    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathcal{O}(|\mathscr{B}|)$.

<!-- defn-14: body_md -->
\label{def:etalements}
    For a vu-functor $F : \mathscr{X}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathscr{Y}$ and $A\in\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{Y})$, \emph{the topological étalement} of $F$ above $A$ is the vu-functor of vu-posets given by $|F/A| : |F^*\mathscr{A}|   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  |\mathscr{A}|$.

    	{F^*\mathscr{A}} & {\mathscr{A}} \\

<!-- rmk-13: body_md -->
Note that if $\mathscr{Y}$ does not have enough vu-sheaves, the topological étalements of $F$ are not enough to recover interesting information on $F$.
<!-- end rmk-13 -->
<!-- prop-11: body_md -->
\label{prop:etalements}\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate} 
        \item\label{prop:etalements:i}
        For $\mathscr{X}$ a bounded vu-category and $A\in\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})$, the topological étalement of $\eta_\mathscr{X}:\mathscr{X}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{

 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{pt}(\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X}))$ above $A$ is given by 
        \[\mathscr{A}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{pt}(\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{A})).\]
        \item\label{prop:etalements:ii} For $f : \mathscr{F}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathscr{E}$ a geometric morphism and $A\in\mathscr{E}$, the topological étalement of $\mathsf{pt}(f)$ above $\mathsf{ev}(A)$ is given by

  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{

 \mkern-1mu}  |\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E}/A)|.\]
