<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item By \Cref{thm:etale}\ref{prop:slice-etale}\ref{prop:point-etale}, we have 
        $\mathrm{\acute{E}t}_{\mathsf{ev}(A)}\cong\mathsf{pt}(\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})/A)\cong\mathsf{pt}(\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{A}))$.
        \[\begin{tikzcd}
            \mathscr{A} & {\mathsf{pt}(\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{A}))}\\
            \mathscr{X} & {\mathsf{pt}(\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X}))}
            \arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
            \arrow["{\text{ét}}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
            \arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-1, to=2-2]
            \arrow["{\text{ét}}", from=1-2, to=2-2]
            \arrow["{\eta_\mathscr{X}}", from=2-1, to=2-2]
        \end{tikzcd}\]
        
        \item By \Cref{thm:etale}\ref{prop:point-etale}, we have 
        $\mathrm{\acute{E}t}_{\mathsf{ev}(A)} \cong \mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E}/A)$ and $\mathrm{\acute{E}t}_{\mathsf{ev}(f^*A)} \cong \mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{F}/f^*A)$.
        \[\begin{tikzcd}
        	\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{F}/f^*A) & {\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E}/A)} \\
        	\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E}) & {\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{F})}
        	\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
        	\arrow["{\text{ét}}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
        	\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-1, to=2-2]
        	\arrow["{\text{ét}}", from=1-2, to=2-2]
        	\arrow["{\mathsf{pt}(f)}", from=2-1, to=2-2]
        \end{tikzcd}\qedhere\]
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- nota-4: body_md -->
\label{nota:em}
    We fix $[-] : \mathds{D}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})$ a small diagram of vu-sheaves over $\mathscr{X}$. For $p\in\mathscr{X}$, we denote by $\EuScript{M}_{\mathds{D}}(p)$ the category of elements of the functor $[-]_p : \mathds{D}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{Set}$, and an element $\ell\in\EuScript{M}_{\mathds{D}}(p)$ will be denoted as a pair $\ell = (D_{\ell},\xi_{\ell})$ with $D_\ell\in\mathds{D}$ and $\xi_\ell\in[D_\ell]_p$.
<!-- end nota-4 -->
<!-- defn-15: body_md -->
A diagram $[-] : \mathds{D}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})$ is said \emph{semi-flat} if for any $p$ in $\mathscr{X}$ the posetal reflection of the category $\EuScript{M}_{\mathds{D}}(p)$ is codirected, i.e.,  for any $\xi_0\in [D_0]_p$ and $\xi_1\in [D_1]_p$ there exists $\xi\in [D]$ with maps $D\rightrightarrows D_i$ mapping $\xi$ to $\xi_i$.
<!-- end defn-15 -->
<!-- cor-5: body_md -->
\label{def:lambda}
    For $[-] : \mathds{D}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})$ a semi-flat diagram, we can consider an \emph{initial ultrafilter} on the objects of $\EuScript{M}_{\mathds{D}}(p)$, that is, an ultrafilter $\lambda$ on pairs $(D,\xi)$, with $D\in\mathds{D}$ and $\xi\in [D]_p$, such that for each $\xi_0\in [D_0]_p$, for $\lambda$-all $(D,\xi)$ there exists a $f : D  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  D_0$ such that $[f]_p(\xi) = \xi_0$.
<!-- end cor-5 -->
<!-- lem-9: body_md -->
If $\mathds{D}$ has finite products and $[-] : \mathds{D}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})$ preserves them, then $[-] : \mathds{D}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})$ is semi-flat.
<!-- end lem-9 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
For $\xi_0\in[D_0]_p$ and $\xi_1\in[D_1]_p$, we consider $(\xi_0,\xi_1)\in[D_0\times D_1]_p$, and the two projections show that $(D_0\times D_1,(\xi_0,\xi_1))$ is smaller than both $(D_i,\xi_i)$ in the posetal reflection of $\EuScript{M}_{\mathds{D}}(p)$.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- cor-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:semi-flat-exist}
    Let $\mathds{D}\subseteq \mathscr{E}$ be a small dense full sub-category of a topos $\mathscr{E}$ closed under products. Then the functor $ \mathds{D}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathsf{Sh}(\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E}))$ sending $D\in\mathds{D}$ to the vu-sheaf $\mathsf{ev}(D)$ is a semi-flat diagram separating vu-arrows. 
    
    In particular, for any full sub-vu-category $\mathscr{X}\subseteq\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E})$, one can find a small semi-flat diagram $[-] : \mathds{D}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})$ of vu-sheaves of the form $\mathsf{ev}(E)$, that moreover separates vu-arrows.
<!-- end cor-6 -->
<!-- ex-3: body_md -->
Let $U\in\mathscr{E}$ be a prebound of $\mathscr{E}$ (i.e.,  the corresponding geometric morphism $\mathscr{E}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{Set}[\mathbb{O}]$ is localic). Then the functor $\mathds{N}^{\mathrm{op}}   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathsf{Sh}(\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E}))$ sending $n$ to the vu-sheaf $\mathsf{ev}(U^n)$, is a semi-flat diagram separating vu-arrows (where $\mathds{N}$ denotes the category of integers seen as finite sets and set-functions between them).
     
    One can think of $U_p$ as the underlying set of the model $p$. In that case, the posetal reflection of $\EuScript{M}_{\mathds{D}}(p)$ is given by the poset of finite subsets of $U_p$ (which can be seen as finite sets of $U$-parameters in $p$) ordered by reverse inclusion. Thus, an initial ultrafilter $\lambda$ as in \Cref{def:lambda} can be seen as a ‘finite set of $U$-parameters in $p$ that contains all the elements of $U_p$’.
<!-- end ex-3 -->
<!-- defn-16: body_md -->
A vu-functor $F:\mathscr{X}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathscr{Y}$ is \emph{vu-full} if for $p$ and $(q_s)_{s:\sigma}$ in $\mathscr{X}$, any vu-arrow $g : F(p) \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\sigma}}\mkern-2mu}{F(q_s)}$ can be thickened to be in the image of $F$, i.e.,  there is $\phi : \tau  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \sigma$ and $f:p \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\tau}}\mkern-2mu}{q_{\phi t}}$ such that $F(f) = \phi^*g$.
<!-- end defn-16 -->
<!-- prop-12: body_md -->
\label{taut-ff}
    A vu-functor between taut vu-categories is fully faithful if and only if it is vu-full and faithful.
<!-- end prop-12 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
It is clear that a fully faithful vu-functor is faithful and vu-full. 
     
    Conversely, we take $F:\mathscr{X}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathscr{Y}$ vu-full and faithful between taut vu-categories and $g : F(p) \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\sigma}}\mkern-2mu}F(q_s)$, and we want to show that $g = F(f)$ for some $f:p \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\sigma}}\mkern-2mu}q_s$.
    Vu-fullness gives us $\phi : \tau  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \sigma$ and $h:p \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\tau}}\mkern-2mu}q_{\phi t}$ such that $F(h) = \phi^*g$.
    For any $\psi_1,\psi_2 : \lambda\rightrightarrows\tau$ equalising $\phi$, we have 
    \[F(\psi_1^*h) = \psi_1^*F(h) = \psi_1^*\phi^*g = \psi_2^*\phi^*g = \psi_2^*F(h) = F(\psi_2^*h)\]
    and so $\psi_1^*h = \psi_2^*h$ by faithfulness of $F$.
    Hence, the tautness hypothesis on $\mathscr{X}$ gives us some $f:p \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\sigma}}\mkern-2mu}q_s$ such that $h = \phi^*f$, and we can then write
    \[\phi^*g = F(h) = F(\phi^*f) = \phi^*F(f),\]
    so that $F(f) = g$ by tautness of $\mathscr{Y}$.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- cor-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:vufull-posetal}
    A vu-functor between taut vu-posets is fully faithful if and only if it is vu-full.
<!-- end cor-7 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
A vu-functor between vu-posets is always faithful.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- prop-13: body_md -->
\label{prop:vufull}\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item\label{prop:vufull-topreflection} Vu-full functors are stable under topological reflections.
        \item\label{prop:vufull-pb} Vu-full functors are stable under pullbacks.
        \item\label{prop:vufull-topetalement} Vu-full functors are stable under topological étalements, i.e.,  if $F : \mathscr{X}   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathscr{Y}$ is vu-full, then $|F/A| : |F^*\mathscr{A}|   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{

We suppose given for any $\xi\in [D]_p$ some $f_{\xi} : p \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu

 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\tau_{\xi}}}\mkern-2mu}{q_{\phi_{\xi}t}}$ (with $\phi_{\xi} : \tau_{\xi}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu

    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \sigma$) such that ${f_{\xi}}_*(\xi) = {\phi_{\xi}}^*(g_D(\xi))$.
    We then choose an initial ultrafilter $\lambda$ on $\EuScript{M}_{\mathds{D}}(p)$ as in \ref{def:lambda} and merge the above $f_{\xi}$ along it
    \[f : p  \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{

    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\ell:\lambda}}\mkern-2mu}{(p \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle f_{\xi_\ell}$};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\tau_{\xi_\ell}}}\mkern-2mu}{q_{\phi_{\xi_\ell} t}})}.\]
    For any $\ell_0 = (D_0,\xi_0)$ in $\EuScript{M}_{\mathds{D}}(p)$ (so $\xi_0\in [D_0]_p$), we have $f_*(\xi_0) = ({f_{\xi_\ell}}_*(\xi_0))_{\ell:\lambda}$, and for $\ell:\lambda$ with $\ell=(D,\xi)$, we can assume by initiality of $\lambda$ that $\ell\geq\ell_0$, and so there is a $\gamma : D  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  D_0$ with $[\gamma]_p(\xi) = \xi_0$.
        
    The diagram chase below then shows that ${f_{\xi}}_*(\xi_0) = {\phi_{\xi}}^*g_{D_0}(\xi_0)$.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	&& {\int_{\sigma}[D]_{q_s}} \\
	\xi & {[D]_p} && {\int_{\tau_{\xi}}[D]_{q_{\phi_{\xi} t}}} \\
	&& {\int_{\sigma}[D_0]_{q_s}} \\
	{\xi_0 = [\gamma]_p(\xi)} & {[D_0]_p} && {\int_{\tau_{\xi}}[D_0]_{q_{\phi_{\xi} t}}}
	\arrow["{{\phi_{\xi}}^*}"{description}, from=1-3, to=2-4]
	\arrow["{([\gamma]_{q_{s}})}"{description, pos=0.7}, from=1-3, to=3-3]
	\arrow["\in"{marking, allow upside down}, draw=none, from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow[dashed, maps to, from=2-1, to=4-1]
	\arrow["{g_D}"{description}, from=2-2, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{[\gamma]_p}"{description, pos=0.7}, from=2-2, to=4-2]
	\arrow["{([\gamma]_{q_{\phi_{\xi} t}})}"{description, pos=0.7}, from=2-4, to=4-4]
	\arrow["{{\phi_{\xi}}^*}"{description}, from=3-3, to=4-4]
	\arrow["\in"{marking, allow upside down}, draw=none, from=4-1, to=4-2]
	\arrow["{g_{D_0}}"{description}, from=4-2, to=3-3]
	\arrow["{{f_{\xi}}_*}"{description, pos=0.7}, from=4-2, to=4-4]
    \arrow["{{f_{\xi}}_*}"{description, pos=0.7}, crossing over, from=2-2, to=2-4]
\end{tikzcd}\]
        \begin{align*}
            &{f_{\xi}}_*(\xi_0) \\ &= {f_{\xi}}_*([\gamma]_p(\xi))  \\
            &= [\gamma]_{q_{\phi_{\xi}(t)}}({f_{\xi}}_*(\xi)) \quad\text{naturality of $[\gamma]$} \\
            &= [\gamma]_{q_{\phi_{\xi}(t)}}({\phi_{\xi}}^*g_D(\xi)) \ \text{the top triangle at $\xi$ by construction of $f_{\xi}$} \\
            &= {\phi_{\xi}}^*[\gamma]_{q_{s}}(g_{D}(\xi)) \quad\text{reindexing of ultraproducts} \\
            &= {\phi_{\xi}}^*g_{D_0}([\gamma]_{p}(\xi)) \quad\text{naturality of the $(g_D)$ in $D$}  \\
            &= {\phi_{\xi}}^*g_{D_0}(\xi_0)   
        \end{align*}
        And denoting $\phi : (\ell:\lambda)\cdot\tau_{\xi_\ell} \stackrel{(\phi_{\xi_\ell})}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{

 \mkern-1mu}  \sigma$,
        \[f_*(\xi_0)  = ({f_{\xi_\ell}}_*(\xi_0))_{\ell:\lambda} = ({\phi_{\xi_\ell}}^*g_{D_0}(\xi_0))_{\ell:\lambda} = {\phi}^*g_{D_0}(\xi_0).\qedhere\]

\label{rmk:Barr-categorified}
    \Cref{cor:Barr-taut} ensures that \ref{Barr-categorified:ii} is equivalent to
    \begin{enumerate}\setcounter{enumi}{2}
        \item \label{Barr-categorified:iii} for any $A\subseteq [D]$ sub-vu-sheaf, $g_D$ restricts to a map $A_p   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \int_{s:\sigma}A_{q_s}$,
    \end{enumerate}
    and we recover \Cref{prop:Barr} by looking at the implication \ref{Barr-categorified:iii}$\Rightarrow$\ref{Barr-categorified:i} for the terminal diagram $1  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})$, that is, the diagram pointing on the terminal vu-sheaf.
     
    In this case of the terminal diagram, we can give the following logical interpretation: if any closed formula satisfied by $p$ is also satisfied by the $(q_s)_{s:\sigma}$, then there exists a homomorphism from $p$ into some thickening of $(q_s)_{s:\sigma}$.
     
    The case of a general diagram can be seen as a generalisation allowing parameters: if a $\mathds{D}$-diagram of set-functions from $p$ to $(q_s)_{s:\sigma}$ defined on the underlying sorts prescribed by $\mathds{D}$ respects all the formulas with parameters, then it can be thickened to become a homomorphism of models.
<!-- end rmk-14 -->

 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})\]

<!-- defn-17: body_md -->
A geometric morphism $f:\mathscr{F}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathscr{E}$ is said to be \emph{subhyperconnected} if it can be written as a composite $f = i \circ h$ of $h$ hyperconnected followed by $i$ an embedding.
<!-- end defn-17 -->
<!-- prop-15: body_md -->
\label{shc-localic}\leavevmode 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item\label{shc-localic-i} Subhyperconnected geometric morphisms are stable under localic reflections, and the localic reflection of a subhyperconnected map is an embedding of locales.
                                                               
        \item\label{shc-ref} Subhyperconnected morphisms are stable under pullback.
                                                                                                                                                                          
        \item\label{shc-slices} A geometric morphism $f : \mathscr{F}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathscr{E}$ is subhyperconnected if and only if its localic slices are embeddings of locales, i.e.,  $|f/E|  : |\mathscr{F}/f^*E| \hookrightarrow|\mathscr{E}/E|$ is an embedding of locales for any $E\in\mathscr{E}$.
                                                                                                     
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-15 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item The localic reflection preserves embeddings \cite[A4.6.12]{johnstone:elephant} and sends hyperconnected morphisms to equivalences \cite[A4.6.6]{johnstone:elephant}.
        \item Hyperconnected geometric morphisms are stable under pullbacks \cite[B3.3.7]{johnstone:elephant}, as well as embeddings \cite[A4.5.14(e)]{johnstone:elephant}.
        \item For the non-trivial direction of the last claim, we consider $f = i \circ p$ the surjection--embedding factorisation of $f$
        \[f : \mathscr{F}\stackrel{p}\twoheadrightarrow\mathscr{G}\stackrel{i}\hookrightarrow\mathscr{E}\]
        and we show that $p$ is hyperconnected. 
         
        Let $G\in\mathscr{G}$, we can write the following factorisation, where $E\coloneqq i_*G$ (and so $G = i^*E$ as $i$ is an embedding).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
        \[\begin{tikzcd}
        	{|\mathscr{F}/p^*G| } && {|\mathscr{E}/i_*G| } \\
        	& {|\mathscr{G}/G| }
        	\arrow["{|f/E| }", from=1-1, to=1-3]
        	\arrow["{|p/G| }"', from=1-1, to=2-2]
        	\arrow["{|i/E| }"', from=2-2, to=1-3]
        \end{tikzcd}\]
        By \cite[A4.6.6(vi)]{johnstone:elephant} it is enough to show that $|p/G|  :|\mathscr{F}/p^*G|   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} |\mathscr{G}/G| $ induces an equivalence of locales. The morphism of locales $|p/G| $ is surjective as the localic slice of a surjective geometric morphism (see \Cref{prop:surj-prop} below); moreover, the assumption that $|f/E| $ is an embedding makes $|p/G| $ one too by the cancellation properties of embeddings. As a result $|p/G| $ is an equivalence as a geometric morphism which is both an embedding and a surjection \cite[A4.2.11]{johnstone:elephant}. \qedhere

        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
        
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- lem-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:full-0dim}
    A continuous map of topological spaces is fully faithful (as a morphism of vu-posets) if and only if the morphism of locales it induces is an embedding.
     
    Conversely, a morphism between locales with enough points is an embedding if and only if it induces a fully faithful vu-functor on its points.
<!-- end lem-11 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
An embedding of locales, or an embedding of topological spaces, induces a fully faithful functor on the points by \Cref{cor:emb-ff}. Conversely, if $f : X  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  Y$ is a fully faithful vu-functor between topological spaces seen as vu-posets, then up to equivalence we can suppose that $f$ is an inclusion of a sub-vu-poset of $Y$, and \Cref{prop:opens-are-upsets} shows that the opens of $X$ are exactly the restriction of the opens of $Y$.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- thm-6: body_md -->
\leavevmode\label{thm:vufull}
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item\label{thm:vufull:iii} Let $F : \mathscr{X}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathscr{Y}$ be a vu-full vu-functor between bounded vu-categories, then $\mathsf{Sh}(F)$ is subhyperconnected. 
        \item\label{thm:vufull:i} Let $\mathscr{X}$ be a bounded vu-category, then $\eta_{\mathscr{X}} : \mathscr{X}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{pt}(\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X}))$ is vu-full.
        \item\label{thm:vufull:ii} Let $f: \mathscr{F}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathscr{E}$ be a subhyperconnected geometric morphism, then $\mathsf{pt}(f)$ is vu-full.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end thm-6 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item We show the hypothesis of \Cref{shc-localic}\ref{shc-slices}. We take $B\in\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{Y})$, by \Cref{prop:loc-slice} we have to show that 
        \[\mathcal{O}(|F^*\mathscr{B}|)   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathcal{O}(|\mathscr{B}|)\] is an embedding of locales.
        
        By \Cref{prop:vufull}\ref{prop:vufull-topetalement} $|F^*\mathscr{B}|   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{

    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  |\mathscr{B}|$ is fully faithful, and we conclude by \Cref{lem:full-0dim}.





        \item We show the hypothesis of \Cref{shc-vufull-cor}. We take $A\in\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})$, by \Cref{prop:etalements}\ref{prop:etalements:i} we have to show that 
        \[|\mathscr{A}|  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} |\mathsf{pt}(\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{A}))|\]
        is fully faithful.

        We have
        \[\begin{tikzcd}
        	{|\mathscr{A}|} & {|\mathsf{pt}(\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{A}))|} \\
        	{\mathsf{pt}(\mathcal{O}(|\mathscr{A}|)))} & {\mathsf{pt}(|\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{A})|)}
        	\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
        	\arrow[hook, from=1-1, to=2-1]
        	\arrow[hook, from=1-2, to=2-2]
        	\arrow["{\cong}", from=2-1, to=2-2]
        \end{tikzcd}\]
        where $\mathsf{pt}(\mathcal{O}(|\mathscr{A}|)))\cong \mathsf{pt}(|\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{A})|)$ by \Cref{circular-square}, 
        $|\mathsf{pt}(\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{A}))|\hookrightarrow\mathsf{pt}(|\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{A})|)$ is fully faithful by \Cref{prop:rpt=ptr},
        $|\mathscr{A}|  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{pt}(\mathcal{O}(|\mathscr{A}|)))$ is fully faithful by \Cref{lem:full-0dim},
        and we conclude by cancellative property of fully faithful vu-functors.
        
        \item We will show that $\mathsf{pt}(f)$ satisfies \ref{shc-vufull-cor}. We take $A\in\mathscr{E}$, by \Cref{prop:etalements}\ref{prop:etalements:ii} we have to show that
        \[|\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{F}/f^*A)|   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{

    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  |\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E}/A)|\]
        is fully faithful.

        We have
        \[\begin{tikzcd}
        	{|\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{F}/f^*A)|} & {|\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E}/A)|} \\
        	{\mathsf{pt}(|\mathscr{F}/f^*A|)} & {\mathsf{pt}(|\mathscr{E}/A|)}
        	\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
        	\arrow[hook, from=1-1, to=2-1]
        	\arrow[hook, from=1-2, to=2-2]
        	\arrow[hook, from=2-1, to=2-2]
        \end{tikzcd}\]
        where $|\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{F}/f^*A)|\hookrightarrow\mathsf{pt}(|\mathscr{F}/f^*A|)$ and $|\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E}/A)|\hookrightarrow\mathsf{pt}(|\mathscr{E}/A|)$ are fully faithful by \Cref{prop:rpt=ptr},
        $\mathsf{pt}(|\mathscr{F}/f^*A| )  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}

        and we conclude by cancellative property of fully faithful vu-functors.\qedhere
     \end{enumerate}

  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{

    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E})$ is faithful, and that can be deduced from the composition

  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{

 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{pt}(\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X}))  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};

<!-- defn-18: body_md -->
\label{def:separating-in-vu-pos}
    A collection $A$ of points of a vu-poset (or a topological space) $X$ is said \emph{separating} if any two opens $U \subseteq V$ that agree on $A$ are equal.
<!-- end defn-18 -->
<!-- prop-16: body_md -->
\label{prop:subclosure-topology}
    Let $A$ be a collection of points of a vu-poset (or a topological space) $X$. For $p$ a point of $X$, the following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item every locally closed subspace (intersection of an open and a closed subspace, see \ref{def:open}) containing $p$ meets $A$; \label{cond:subclosure-johnstone}
        \item $p$ belongs to $\operatorname{\mathsf{cl}}(A \cap \operatorname{\mathsf{cl}}\{p\})$; \label{cond:subclosure-closure}
        \item there exists an ultrafamily $(a_s)_{s:\sigma}$ of points in $A$ and a $\sigma$-family of ultrafilters $(\tau_s)_{s:\sigma}$ such that $p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\sigma}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} a_s$ and $a_s  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\tau_s}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} p$ for all $s:\sigma$. If moreover $X$ is taut, we can assume all the $\tau_s$ are trivial. \label{cond:subclosure-vu-arrow}
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-16 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$\ref{cond:subclosure-johnstone}\Leftrightarrow\ref{cond:subclosure-closure}$] By \Cref{lem:smallest-closedset}, $\operatorname{\mathsf{cl}}\{p\}$ is the smallest closed subspace containing $p$, so \ref{cond:subclosure-johnstone} is equivalent to
        \[\text{for all open } U\text{ containing }p,\ U\cap\operatorname{\mathsf{cl}}\{p\}\text{ intersects } A,\]
        which by \ref{lem:closure} means $p\in\operatorname{\mathsf{cl}}(A\cap\operatorname{\mathsf{cl}}\{p\})$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
        \item[$\ref{cond:subclosure-closure}\Leftrightarrow\ref{cond:subclosure-vu-arrow}$]
        Follows directly from \Cref{def:open}. \qedhere
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- defn-19: body_md -->
\label{def:poset-subcl}
    If the above condition is satisfied we say that \emph{$p$ is in the subclosure of $A$}, and we denote by $\operatorname{\mathsf{scl}}(A)\subseteq X$ the collection of $p$ that are in the subclosure of $A$.
    Concretely, $p\in\operatorname{\mathsf{scl}}(A)$ if there exists a $\sigma$-family $(a_s)_{s:\sigma}$ of points in $A$ and a $\sigma$-family of ultrafilters $(\tau_s)_{s:\sigma}$ such that $p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\sigma}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} a_s$ and $a_s  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\tau_s}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} p$ for $s:\sigma$.
<!-- end defn-19 -->
<!-- rmk-15: body_md -->
The condition \ref{cond:subclosure-johnstone} shows that if $X$ is the vu-poset of points of a topological space we recover the definition of Johnstone \cite[before Lem.~2.1]{johnstone-1980:open-maps}. The condition \ref{cond:subclosure-vu-arrow} is an equivalent formulation from the vu-posetal point of view, it is the one we will use to categorify the notion of subclosure.
<!-- end rmk-15 -->
<!-- prop-17: body_md -->
\label{prop:subcl-sep-topological-case}
    A collection of points $A$ of a vu-poset $X$ is separating if and only if its subclosure is $X$.
<!-- end prop-17 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
We suppose that $\operatorname{\mathsf{scl}}(A) = X$ and we show that $A$ is separating. Let $U$ and $V$ be two opens which agree on $A$, and pick $p \in U$, we want to show $p\in V$.
    By assumption, there exists $(a_s)_{s:\sigma}$ in $A$ such that $p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\sigma}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} a_s$ and $a_s  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\tau_s}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} p$.
    From $p  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\sigma}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} a_s$ and $p \in U$, it follows that for $s:\sigma$, we have $a_s \in U$ and so $a_s \in V$.
    In particular there exists at least one $s_0$ such that $a_{s_0} \in V$ and $a_{s_0}  \mathrel{\preccurlyeq_{{\tau_{s_0}}}^{{}}\mkern-2mu} p$, which guarantees $p \in V$. This shows $U \subseteq V$, and by symmetry the reverse also holds.

    Conversely, we suppose that $A$ is separating in $X$. By \Cref{lem:closure}, it is enough to show that any open $U$ containing $p$ intersects $A\cap \operatorname{\mathsf{cl}}\{p\}$.
    As $U \setminus \operatorname{\mathsf{cl}}\{p\}$ is an open strictly contained in $U$, it must be separated from $U$ by some $a\in A$. In other words, there exists $a \in A$ such that $a \in U$ and $a\in\operatorname{\mathsf{cl}}\{p\}$, hence $U$ intersects $A\cap \operatorname{\mathsf{cl}}\{p\}$ as wanted.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- defn-20: body_md -->

<!-- prop-18: body_md -->
\label{prop:presheaf-separating-retract}
    Let $\mathscr{C}$ be a small category seen as a vu-category (see \cite[4.2(vi)]{Saa}),
     
    then $\mathds{A}\subseteq\mathsf{Ob}(\mathscr{C})$ is separating if and only if every object of $\mathscr{C}$ is a retract of an object of $\mathds{A}$.
<!-- end prop-18 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
The category of vu-sheaves above $\mathscr{C}$ is precisely the presheaf topos $\mathsf{Set}^{\mathscr{C}}$.
     
    Hence, this follows from \cite[A4.2.7(b)]{johnstone:elephant},
     
    by noticing that a set of objects of $\mathscr{C}$ separates $\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{C})$ if and only if it induces a separating set of points of the presheaf topos $\mathsf{Set}^{\mathscr{C}}$.
<!-- end proof-38 -->

<!-- ex-4: body_md -->
\leavevmode\label{ex:vu-retract}
    We can recover our two motivating examples.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item In a topological space $T$, a point $p$ is a vu-retract of points in $A \subseteq X$ precisely if it belongs to $\operatorname{\mathsf{scl}}(A)$ (see \Cref{def:poset-subcl}).

    \end{enumerate}
    Here are some more interesting, and maybe unexpected, examples.

<!-- rmk-16: body_md -->
We believe that, assuming $\mathscr{X}$ taut, one can fully characterize such filtered colimits (in the above vu-categorical sense) by means of vu-retracts. This would imply that in the context of taut vu-categories, filtered colimits are \emph{absolute}, thereby explaining why vu-functors between vu-categories of points of toposes automatically preserve filtered colimits. Note that a particular case of this fact has already been observed in \cite[5.3.4]{Lurie}.
<!-- end rmk-16 -->
<!-- rmk-17: body_md -->
It is worth noting that a characterisation of soberness by nets for topological spaces has been given in \cite{Nets}. The author uses nets instead of filters, but we can make the following analogies: an ‘observative net’ corresponds to some yet-to-be-defined notion of ‘vu-idempotent’, and ‘strongly convergence’ corresponds to some ‘splitting’ of it. Moreover, the ‘b-topology’ is the topology generated by the locally closed sets, connecting the ‘b-closure’ to the subclosure.
<!-- end rmk-17 -->
<!-- defn-22: body_md -->
\label{def:cat-subcl}
    The \emph{subclosure} of a collection $\mathds{A}$ of objects of a vu-category $\mathscr{X}$ is the full sub-vu-category consisting of the points which are vu-retracts of points in $\mathds{A}$. We will denote it by $\operatorname{\mathsf{scl}}_\mathscr{X}(\mathds{A})\subseteq\mathscr{X}$, or just $\operatorname{\mathsf{scl}}(\mathds{A})$ if clear from context.
<!-- end defn-22 -->
<!-- rmk-18: body_md -->
\label{rmk:subclosure-Tref}
    The above notion is a categorification of \Cref{def:poset-subcl} in the sense that for vu-posets we recover the already defined notion. 
     
    Not only is it true that $\operatorname{\mathsf{scl}}_X(A) = \operatorname{\mathsf{scl}}_{\iota(X)}(A)$, as we have noted, but also $\operatorname{\mathsf{scl}}_{\mathscr{X}}(\mathds{A}) \subseteq \operatorname{\mathsf{scl}}_{|\mathscr{X}|}(\mathds{A})$, although the inclusion is strict in general as we ask for an additional coherence.
<!-- end rmk-18 -->
<!-- prop-19: body_md -->
\label{vu-retract-direction-facile}
    If all points of $\mathscr{X}$ are vu-retracts of points in $\mathds{A}$ then $\mathds{A}$ is separating.
<!-- end prop-19 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
The category $\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})$ is a pretopos, so to show that $(\mathsf{ev}_a)_{a:\mathds{A}}:\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{Set}^{\mathds{A}}$ is conservative it is enough to show that it is faithful.
    Let $f$ and $g$ be two parallel maps $A \rightrightarrows B$ in $\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})$ which agree on all points $a\in \mathds{A}$, we need to show that $f = g$. For $p \in \mathscr{X}$, we choose a vu-retraction $i : p  \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\sigma}}\mkern-2mu} a_s$ and $(r_s : a_s  \mathrel{{ \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{

    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\tau_s}}\mkern-2mu} p)_{s:\sigma}$ with the $(a_s)_{s:\sigma}$ in $\mathds{A}$ and we consider the following diagram of sets.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{A_p} & {B_p} & \\
	{\int_{\sigma}A_{a_s}} & {\int_{\sigma}B_{a_s}} & {\int_{\sigma}\int_{\tau_s}B_p}
	\arrow["{f_p}"{description}, curve={height=-6pt}, dashed, from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{g_p}"{description}, curve={height=6pt}, dashed, from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{i_*}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{i_*}"', from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow["\delta", hook, from=1-2, to=2-3]
	\arrow[""{name=0, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, "{(f_{a_s})}", curve={height=-6pt}, from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow[""{name=1, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, "{(g_{a_s})}"', curve={height=6pt}, from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{({r_s}_*)}"', from=2-2, to=2-3]
	\arrow[between={0.2}{0.8}, equals, from=0, to=1]
\end{tikzcd}\]
    The right triangle commutes by definition of a vu-retraction and the left square commutes by naturality. Since the diagonal $\delta$ is an injection, it follows that $f_p = g_p$, as desired.

<!-- nota-5: body_md -->
Let $\mathds{A}$ be a collection of points of a vu-category $\mathscr{X}$.
    Given a vu-sheaf $Y \in\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})$ we denote its total space by $\mathscr{Y}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathscr{X}$, and we denote by $\mathds{A}_Y$ the collection of points of $\mathscr{Y}$ that lie above a point in $\mathds{A}$, i.e.,                                 
    $\mathds{A}_Y$ consists of the pairs $(a, y)$ with $a \in \mathds{A}$ and $y \in Y(a)$.
<!-- end nota-5 -->
<!-- lem-12: body_md -->
\label{prop:separating-slice}
     If $\mathds{A}$ is a separating collection of points of $\mathscr{X}$, then $\mathds{A}_Y$ is a separating collection of points in $\mathscr{Y}$.
<!-- end lem-12 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
Let $f: A   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu

    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  B$ be a map of sheaves $\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{Y})$ that is an isomorphism on the points of $\mathds{A}_Y$, i.e.,  for any $a\in\mathds{A}$ and $y\in Y_a$ the map $f_{(a,y)} : A_{(a,y)}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{

    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}

    We have $\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})/Y \cong \mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{Y})$ by \Cref{thm:etale}\ref{prop:slice-etale}, this allows us to see $f$ as a map in $\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})$. Concretely, we have the following diagram of étale vu-functors.
                                                                                                                                                                                 
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        \mathscr{A} && \mathscr{B} \\

        \arrow["f", from=1-1, to=1-3]
        \arrow["{\pi_A}"', from=1-1, to=2-2]
        \arrow["{\pi_B}", from=1-3, to=2-2]
        \arrow["{\pi_Y}", from=2-2, to=3-2]

    As $\mathds{A}$ is separating in $\mathscr{X}$, it is enough to show that $f: \mathscr{A}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{

    But for any point $a\in\mathds{A}$, the map on the stalks at $a$ is given by 
    \[\textstyle\sum_{y\in Y(a)}A_{(a,y)}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{

 \mkern-1mu} \sum_{y\in Y(a)}B_{(a,y)}\]

  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{

    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  B_{(a,y)})_{y\in Y(a)}$ that are all bijections by assumption.

    \draw[cd-arrow-style,ulttip] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}}\mkern2mu_{{\tau_\ell}}\mkern-2mu} p).\]
        
        Since the $[-] : \mathds{D}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})$ separates vu-arrows, it suffices to check that each sheaf in $\mathds{D}$ sends $j_\ell \circ_\lambda \delta $ and the diagonal to the same map of sets, that is, that for any $\ell_0 = (D_0,\xi_0) \in \EuScript{M}_\mathds{D}(p)$, the ultrafamily $(j_\ell \circ_\lambda \delta)_*(\xi_0) = \left({j_\ell}_*(\xi_{0})\right)_{\ell : \lambda}$ is the constant ultrafamily $((\xi_0)_{\tau_\ell})_{\ell:\lambda}$.
        
        We thus fix $\ell_0 = (D_0,\xi_0)$ in $\EuScript{M}_\mathds{D}(p)$,                                                                                                       
        and we show that ${j_\ell}_*(\xi_0)$ is the constant $\tau_\ell$-family at $\xi_0$ for all $\ell : \lambda$.
         
        By assumption on $\lambda$, we can assume that for all $\ell : \lambda$ there exists $\gamma : \ell   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \ell_0$, i.e.,  $\gamma : D_\ell   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  D_{0}$ such that $[\gamma]_p(\xi_\ell) = \xi_{0}$, and we consider the following naturality square of $j_\ell$, which shows ${j_\ell}_*([\gamma]_p(\xi_\ell)) = ([\gamma]_p)_{\tau_\ell} ({j_\ell}_*(\xi_{\ell}))$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
        \[\begin{tikzcd}
        	{\xi_\ell} & {[D_\ell]_p} & {\int_{\tau_\ell} [D_\ell]_p} & {} \\
        	{\xi_{0} = [\gamma]_p(\xi_\ell)} & {[D_{0}]_p} & {\int_{\tau_\ell}[D_{0}]_p}
        	\arrow["\in"{description}, draw=none, from=1-1, to=1-2]
        	\arrow[dashed, maps to, from=1-1, to=2-1]
        	\arrow["{{j_\ell}_*}", from=1-2, to=1-3]
        	\arrow["{[\gamma]_p}"', from=1-2, to=2-2]
        	\arrow["{([\gamma]_p)_{\tau_\ell}}", from=1-3, to=2-3]
        	\arrow["\in"{description}, draw=none, from=2-1, to=2-2]
        	\arrow["{{j_\ell}_*}"', from=2-2, to=2-3]
        \end{tikzcd}\]
        We conclude: 
        \begin{align*}
            {j_\ell}_*(\xi_{0}) &= {j_\ell}_*([\gamma]_p(\xi_\ell)) & \\
            &= ([\gamma]_p)_{\tau_\ell} ({j_\ell}_*(\xi_{\ell})) &\text{naturality of $j_\ell$} \\
            &= ([\gamma]_p)_{\tau_\ell} ((\xi_\ell)_{\tau_\ell}) & \text{assumption of \ref{prop:ultraretract-crux-iii}}\\
            &= ([\gamma]_p (\xi_\ell))_{\tau_\ell} & \\
            &= (\xi_{0})_{\tau_\ell}. &  \qedhere   
        \end{align*} 

    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- cor-12: body_md -->
\label{cor:ultraretract}
    Let $\mathscr{X}\subseteq\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E})$ be a full sub-vu-category of $\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E})$, and $\mathds{A}$ a collection of points of $\mathscr{X}$. Then $\operatorname{\mathsf{scl}}_\mathscr{X}(\mathds{A}) = \mathscr{X}$ if and only if $\operatorname{\mathsf{scl}}_{|\mathscr{Y}|}(\mathds{A}_{Y}) = |\mathscr{Y}|$ for any $Y = \mathsf{ev}(E)\in\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})$, $E\in\mathscr{E}$.
<!-- end cor-12 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
Follows from \Cref{prop:ultraretract-crux} above and \Cref{prop:semi-flat-exist}.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- thm-8: body_md -->
\label{prop:subcl-sep-categorified}
    Let $\mathscr{X}\subseteq\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E})$ be a full sub-vu-category of $\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E})$, and $\mathds{A}$ a collection of points of $\mathscr{X}$. Then $\mathds{A}$ is separating if and only if $\operatorname{\mathsf{scl}}_\mathscr{X}(\mathds{A}) = \mathscr{X}$.
<!-- end thm-8 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
It is a sufficient condition by \Cref{vu-retract-direction-facile}, we now show that it is necessary, we suppose $\mathds{A}$ separating and show that $\operatorname{\mathsf{scl}}_X(\mathds{A}) = \mathscr{X}$. By \Cref{cor:ultraretract} and \Cref{prop:subcl-sep-topological-case}, it is sufficient to show that $\mathds{A}_{Y}$ is separating in $|\mathscr{Y}|$ for any $Y = \mathsf{ev}(E)$, $E\in\mathscr{E}$. But for each $E$, the collection of points $\mathds{A}_{Y}$ is separating in $\mathscr{Y}$ by \Cref{prop:separating-slice}, and so, a fortiori, separating in $|\mathscr{Y}|$.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- defn-23: body_md -->
\label{def:vu-subdense}
    A vu-functor $F : \mathscr{X}   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathscr{Y}$ is \emph{vu-subdense} if the subclosure of its image $F(\mathscr{X}) \subseteq \mathscr{Y}$ is the whole of $\mathscr{Y}$,
    \[\operatorname{\mathsf{scl}}_\mathscr{Y}(F(X)) = \mathscr{Y},\]
    i.e.,  if any point of $\mathscr{Y}$ is a vu-retract of an ultrafamily of points in the image of $F$.
<!-- end defn-23 -->
<!-- prop-21: body_md -->
\label{prop:vu-subdense-topological}
    Let $f : X   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  Y$ be a functor of topological spaces (or equivalently, essentially small taut vu-posets), the following assertions are equivalent:
     
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item \label{prop:vu-subdense-topological-i} 
        $f$ is vu-subdense; 
         
        \item \label{prop:vu-subdense-topological-ii} 
        $f^{-1} : \mathcal{P}(Y)   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathcal{P}(X)$ takes non-empty locally closed sets to non-empty locally closed sets; 
         
        \item \label{prop:vu-subdense-topological-iii} 
        $f^* : \mathcal{O}(Y)   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathcal{O}(X)$ preserves the order \emph{strictly}, that is $f$ induces a surjection of locales.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-21 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[\ref{prop:vu-subdense-topological-i}$\Rightarrow$\ref{prop:vu-subdense-topological-ii}] 
        If $A$ is a non-empty locally closed set of $Y$, then $A$ must meet $f(X)$ non-trivially, that is, $f^{-1}(A)$ is non-empty, and it is clearly locally closed since $f$ is continuous.  
         
        \item[\ref{prop:vu-subdense-topological-ii}$\Rightarrow$\ref{prop:vu-subdense-topological-iii}] 
        If $U \subsetneq V$ in $\mathcal{O}(Y)$, then $(Y \setminus U) \cap V$ is a non-empty locally closed set, hence so is its image under $f^{-1}$. That is, $f^*(U) \subsetneq f^*(V)$.
         
        \item[\ref{prop:vu-subdense-topological-iii}$\Rightarrow$\ref{prop:vu-subdense-topological-i}] 
        This is a reformulation of \Cref{prop:subcl-sep-topological-case}.\qedhere
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- prop-22: body_md -->
\label{prop:subdense-stability}\leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item\label{prop:subdense-stability:o} Let $F :\mathscr{X}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathscr{Y}$ and $G:\mathscr{Y}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathscr{Z}$ be vu-functors.
        If $F$ and $G$ are vu-subdense then so is $G\circ F$. If $G\circ F$ is vu-subdense then so is $G$. And if $G\circ F$ is vu-subdense and $G$ is fully faithful then so is $F$. 
        \item\label{prop:subdense-stability:i} Vu-subdense functors are stable under topological reflection.
        \item\label{prop:subdense-stability:ii} Vu-subdense functors are stable under pullback along étale functors, i.e.,  if $F : \mathscr{X}   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathscr{Y}$ is vu-subdense, so is $F/A : F^*\mathscr{A}   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathscr{A}$ for each $A \in \mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{Y})$.
        \item\label{prop:subdense-stability:iii} Vu-subdense functors are stable under topological étalements (see \Cref{def:etalements}), i.e.,  if $F : \mathscr{X}   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathscr{Y}$ is vu-subdense, so is $|F/A| : |F^*\mathscr{A}|   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  |\mathscr{A}|$ for each $A \in \mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{Y})$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-22 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
\ref{prop:subdense-stability:o} is clear,
        \ref{prop:subdense-stability:i} is a consequence of \Cref{rmk:subclosure-Tref}, \ref{prop:subdense-stability:ii} follows from \Cref{lem:subcl-etalement},                                                                                                                                                                                                             
        and \ref{prop:subdense-stability:iii} follows from the previous two.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- prop-23: body_md -->
\label{prop:vu-subdense-slice}
    Let $\mathscr{Y} \subseteq \mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E})$ be a full sub-vu-category of $\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E})$. A vu-functor $F : \mathscr{X}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathscr{Y}$ is vu-subdense if and only if all its topological étalements above sheaves from $\mathscr{E}$ are vu-subdense, i.e.,   $|F/A| : |F^*\mathscr{A}|   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  |\mathscr{A}|$ is vu-subdense for any $A = \mathsf{ev}(E) \in \mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{Y})$ with $E\in\mathscr{E}$.
<!-- end prop-23 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
The direct direction was just shown in \Cref{prop:subdense-stability}, and the converse follows from \Cref{cor:ultraretract}.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- prop-24: body_md -->
\leavevmode\label{prop:surj-prop}
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item\label{prop:surj-prop:i} Geometric surjections are stable under localic reflection.
        \item\label{prop:surj-prop:ii} Geometric surjections morphisms are stable under pullback along étale geometric morphisms.
                                                                                                    
        \item\label{prop:surj-prop:iv} A geometric morphism $f : \mathscr{F}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathscr{E}$ is surjective if and only if its localic slices (see \Cref{def:loc-slice}) are surjections of locales, i.e.,  $|f/E|  : |\mathscr{F}/f^*E|   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} |\mathscr{E}/E|$                                                                                  
        is a surjection of locales for any $E\in\mathscr{E}$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-24 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
The claim \ref{prop:surj-prop:i} is exactly \cite[A4.6.12]{johnstone:elephant},
    claim \ref{prop:surj-prop:ii} follows from inspection or \cite[C3.1.24]{johnstone:elephant} (take a discrete internal category there),
    and \ref{prop:surj-prop:iv} is a reformulation of \cite[VII.4, Lem.~3]{mac-lane-moerdijk}.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- lem-14: body_md -->
\label{lem:surj-0dim}\leavevmode    
                                                                                
                      
                                                                                            
                                                                                             
                                                                                              
                    
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item\label{lem:surj-0dim:i}\label{lem:surj-0dim:iii} A vu-functor between topological spaces is vu-subdense if and only if it induces a surjection of locales. In particular the sobrification $X  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{pt}(\mathcal{O}(X))$ is a vu-subdense embedding. 
        \item\label{lem:surj-0dim:ii} For any topos with enough points $\mathscr{E}$, the vu-functor $|\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E})|  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{pt}(|\mathscr{E}|)$ is a vu-subdense embedding.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-14 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
\ref{lem:surj-0dim:i} follows easily from \Cref{prop:vu-subdense-topological}. The vu-functor $|\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E})|  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{pt}(|\mathscr{E}|)$ is fully faithful by \Cref{prop:rpt=ptr}, so it only remains to show that is it vu-subdense. For that, it is enough to notice that the points of $\mathscr{E}$ induce a separating class of points of $|\mathscr{E}|$ (because $\mathscr{E}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle \ \,$};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->>] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} |\mathscr{E}|$ is surjective and $\mathscr{E}$ is assumed to have enough points).
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- thm-9: body_md -->
\leavevmode\label{thm:surj}
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Let $F : \mathscr{X}  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{

 \mkern-1mu} \mathscr{Y}$ be a vu-subdense vu-functor between bounded vu-categories, then $\mathsf{Sh}(F)$ is surjective.

  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{

 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{pt}(\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X}))$ is vu-subdense.

  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{

<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
\leavevmode
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item We show the hypothesis of \Cref{prop:surj-prop}\ref{prop:surj-prop:iv}. We take $B\in\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{Y})$, by \Cref{prop:loc-slice} we have to show that 
        \[\mathcal{O}(|F^*\mathscr{B}|)   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathcal{O}(|\mathscr{B}|)\] is a surjection of locales.
        
        By \Cref{prop:subdense-stability}\ref{prop:subdense-stability:iii} $|F^*\mathscr{B}|   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  |\mathscr{B}|$ is vu-subdense, and we conclude by \Cref{lem:surj-0dim}\ref{lem:surj-0dim:iii}.

        \item We show the hypothesis of \Cref{prop:vu-subdense-slice}. We take $A\in\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{X})$, by \Cref{prop:etalements}\ref{prop:etalements:i} we have to show that 
        \[|\mathscr{A}|  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} |\mathsf{pt}(\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{A}))|\]
        is vu-subdense.
        
                                                                         
                                                                                                                 

        We have
        \[\begin{tikzcd}
        	{|\mathscr{A}|} & {|\mathsf{pt}(\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{A}))|} \\
        	{\mathsf{pt}(\mathcal{O}(|\mathscr{A}|)))} & {\mathsf{pt}(|\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{A})|)}
        	\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
        	\arrow["{\text{vu-subd.}}"', hook, from=1-1, to=2-1]
        	\arrow[hook, from=1-2, to=2-2]
        	\arrow["{\cong}", from=2-1, to=2-2]
        \end{tikzcd}\]
        where $\mathsf{pt}(\mathcal{O}(|\mathscr{A}|)))\cong \mathsf{pt}(|\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{A})|)$ by \Cref{circular-square}, 
        $|\mathsf{pt}(\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{A}))|\hookrightarrow\mathsf{pt}(|\mathsf{Sh}(\mathscr{A})|)$ is an embedding by \Cref{prop:rpt=ptr},
        $|\mathscr{A}|  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu} \mathsf{pt}(\mathcal{O}(|\mathscr{A}|)))$ is vu-subdense by \Cref{lem:surj-0dim}\ref{lem:surj-0dim:i},
        and we conclude by \Cref{prop:subdense-stability}\ref{prop:subdense-stability:o}.

        \item We will show that $\mathsf{pt}(f)$ satisfies \ref{prop:vu-subdense-slice}. We take $A\in\mathscr{E}$, by \Cref{prop:etalements}\ref{prop:etalements:ii} we have to show that
        \[|\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{F}/f^*A)|   \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  |\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E}/A)|\]
        is vu-subdense.
        
        We have
        \[\begin{tikzcd}
        	{|\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{F}/f^*A)|} & {|\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E}/A)|} \\
        	{\mathsf{pt}(|\mathscr{F}/f^*A|)} & {\mathsf{pt}(|\mathscr{E}/A|)}
        	\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
        	\arrow["{\text{vu-subd.}}"', hook, from=1-1, to=2-1]
        	\arrow[hook, from=1-2, to=2-2]
        	\arrow["{\text{vu-subd.}}", from=2-1, to=2-2]
        \end{tikzcd}\]
        where $|\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{F}/f^*A)|\hookrightarrow\mathsf{pt}(|\mathscr{F}/f^*A|)$ is a vu-subdense embedding by \Cref{lem:surj-0dim}\ref{lem:surj-0dim:ii},
        $|\mathsf{pt}(\mathscr{E}/A)|\hookrightarrow\mathsf{pt}(|\mathscr{E}/A|)$ is an embedding by \Cref{prop:rpt=ptr},
        $\mathsf{pt}(|\mathscr{F}/f^*A| )  \mathrel{\mkern-1mu
  \tikz[baseline={([yshift=-0.58ex]a.south)}]{ 
    \node[minimum width=1em,align=center,inner xsep=0.5ex,inner ysep=0.25ex] (a) {$\scriptstyle $};
    \draw[cd-arrow-style,->] (a.south west) -- (a.south east);}
 \mkern-1mu}  \mathsf{pt}(|\mathscr{E}/A|)$ is vu-subdense by \Cref{prop:surj-prop}\ref{prop:surj-prop:iv} and \Cref{lem:surj-0dim},
        and we conclude by \Cref{prop:subdense-stability}\ref{prop:subdense-stability:o}.
        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
        
                                                                                                                                               
        \qedhere
     \end{enumerate}

<!-- rmk-19: body_md -->
\label{cor:vu-subdense:counterex}
    When the codomain of $F$ does not have enough sheaves, does $\mathsf{Sh}(F)$ being surjective entail that $F$ is vu-subdense? We expect that answering this question requires a better algebraic understanding of vu-retractions in non-sober vu-categories, which we defer to future work.
<!-- end rmk-19 -->
